questionText: Which of the following regular expressions represent(s) the set of all binary numbers that are divisible by three? Assume that the string $\epsilon$ is divisible by three.
explanation:
Step 1: Construct DFA for binary numbers divisible by 3
Let states be $q_0, q_1, q_2$ representing remainders $0, 1, 2$ modulo $3$, respectively.
• Transitions from $q_0$: on '0' $\to q_0$, on '1' $\to q_1$
• Transitions from $q_1$: on '0' $\to q_2$, on '1' $\to q_0$
• Transitions from $q_2$: on '0' $\to q_1$, on '1' $\to q_2$
Here, $q_0$ is both the start state and the only final state.

Step 2: State Elimination to find Regular Expressions

Case 1: Eliminating state $q_2$ first
• The self-loop at $q_2$ is $1$.
• The path $q_1 \to q_2 \to q_1$ creates a loop at $q_1$ with expression $01^*0$.
• Total loop at $q_1$ becomes $(01^*0)^*$.
• The path $q_0 \to q_1 \dots \to q_0$ gives $1(01^*0)^*1$.
• Combining with self-loop $0$ at $q_0$, the expression is $(0 + 1(01^*0)^*1)^*$.
This matches Option (A).

Case 2: Using standard regular expression equivalence
Using the identity $(X + Y)^* = (X^* Y^*)^*$, with $X = 0$ and $Y = 1(01^*0)^*1$, we get:
$(0 + 1(01^*0)^*1)^* = (0^* (1(01^*0)^*1)^*)^*$.
This matches Option (C).

Case 3: Eliminating state $q_1$ first
• Path $q_0 \to q_1 \to q_0$ gives loop $11$ at $q_0$.
• Path $q_0 \to q_1 \to q_2$ gives transition $10$.
• Path $q_2 \to q_1 \to q_0$ gives transition $01$.
• Self-loop at $q_2$ becomes $1 + 00$.
• Path $q_0 \to q_2 \dots \to q_0$ gives $10(1+00)^*01$.
• Combining all loops at $q_0$ gives $(0 + 11 + 10(1+00)^*01)^*$.
This matches Option (B).

Option (D) incorrectly has $00$ at the end instead of $01$, so it is incorrect.

Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.
